title: Calibration run ephemeral snapshots & delegated access handover for FP8/INT8 validation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Define and implement a first-class lifecycle for calibration job runs and their artifacts in Redwood Console that supports ephemeral snapshots (TTL-driven), controlled handover of artifacts for external review, and accuracy-gated promotion for FP8 and INT8 quantization profiles. The goal is to reduce storage cost, improve auditability for regulated customers, and enable safe delegated access during model validation without creating long-lived, ungoverned artifacts.
background: Calibration campaigns for multi-tenant customers generate many intermediate artifacts: traces, calibration histograms, per-layer calibration tables, and quant profiles (FP8/INT8). Currently artifacts are stored indefinitely or require manual cleanup. Customers and internal teams have asked for: 1) TTL policies per run, 2) a secure way to share ephemeral artifacts with auditors or model owners, 3) explicit accuracy gating to prevent regressions when promoting quant profiles to production variants. There have been multiple cost spikes and at least one compliance audit finding related to long-lived developmental artifacts.
scope:
- Controlled lifecycle for calibration runs and their artifacts (snapshots, logs, quant profiles).
- UI controls in Console to configure per-run TTL and retention tiers (ephemeral, short-term, permanent).
- Delegated access tokens and one-click signed export links for temporary reviewer access.
- Accuracy gating: configurable metric thresholds (e.g., perplexity delta, token-level error rates) and an automated promotion path when thresholds are met.
- Audit logging of all access, exports, promotions, and GC events.
- RBAC surface for who can extend TTLs, promote artifacts, and request exports.
out_of_scope:
- Re-architecting the calibration executor itself (compute optimizations).
- Cross-tenant artifact sharing beyond delegated read-only exports.
- Long-term cold storage tiering costs (billing will be handled by a separate initiative).
proposed_solution:
1) Run snapshot model: when a calibration run completes, create a signed, immutable snapshot object with metadata (run_id, model_version, profile_type FP8/INT8, metrics).
2) Allow per-run TTL (default 30d ephemeral) with auto-GC; UI and API to extend or pin snapshots.
3) Delegated access: create time-limited, signed access tokens (link-based) with scope read-only and optional download bundle. Tokens appear in the run timeline and can be revoked; creation requires permission.
4) Accuracy gating: add a promotion workflow that evaluates run metrics against a configurable threshold set attached to the target model alias. Promotion writes promotion events to audit and creates a signed promoted-artifact tag.
5) Audit & retention: every snapshot action (create, export, extend, revoke, promote, GC) produces an audit record (user, ip, action, timestamp) surfaced in Console and exported to customer audit logs (when enabled).
acceptance_criteria: Console: per-run TTL selector visible on run summary and configurable via API
Default TTL set to 30 days for ephemeral snapshots; system GC reclaims artifacts after TTL without manual intervention
Delegated access links are single-use or time-limited and revocable; creation requires 'can_create_exports' RBAC permission
Promotion workflow enforces accuracy gates: attempt to promote a quant profile that fails threshold must be blocked and logged
Audit trail contains action, actor, run_id, artifact_id, and IP; logs exportable to customer S3/KMS integration
E2E tests cover run snapshot creation, TTL expiry, link issuance, link revocation, and promotion success/failure paths
Security review completed and any cryptographic signing using customer KMS keys verified in Private deployments
testing_plan: Unit tests for snapshot metadata creation and TTL enforcement
Integration tests: simulate calibration runs (FP8/INT8), assert artifact bundle created and accessible via link
Security tests: link forgery/resilience, revocation behavior, signed export verification
Load test: create 10k ephemeral snapshots and run GC cycle to validate throughput and S3/listing performance
User acceptance: PM + Design review of Console flows with sample customer (ACME Health)
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal beta): feature behind feature-flag for Redwood internal teams and early adopter customers
Phase 2 (selected customers): opt-in for customers with calibration volume > X/month; gather feedback and telemetry
Phase 3 (general availability): enable default TTL, RBAC enforced; announce in release notes and migration guide
Migration: provide a one-time bulk 'pin' tool for customers to mark existing artifacts as permanent before GA
audit_logging_requirements: Record: action, actor, artifact_id, run_id, model_version, metrics snapshot at time of action
Retention of audit logs configurable per-customer (default 365 days)
Forward audit entries to customer-preferred sink (S3, Splunk, Datadog) when configured
Tamper-evident signing of promotion and export events in Private deployments using customer KMS
migration_notes: Existing artifacts older than new default TTL should not be auto-deleted until a migration window; provide 'pin' CLI and Console flow
Create backend job to backfill snapshot metadata for historical runs to enable TTL application
Communicate with customers 30 days prior to any cleanup GC run that will remove artifacts older than new TTL
